recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless a future work group decision changes the slicing model or removes openAtEnd.
issue_request: FHIR-5581 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core datatypes request to add language discouraging openAtEnd because ordered slicing creates interoperability issues.
initial_application: The imported SVN history includes git commit 8349666a9e471630178f9caa97d3452153062d54, matching Jira's svn 4491 comment, which added the current openAtEnd warning to source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml.
additional_context: ElementDefinition is active and normative in source/fhir.ini. The active SlicingRules binding points to #resource-slicing-rules, where the openAtEnd row says it requires ordered slices, makes sharing uses hard, and should only be done where absolutely required. Later FHIR-34142 added a warning invariant for openAtEnd or ordered slicing when orderMeaning is absent, reinforcing the same caution.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the authoritative source already contains the requested discouraging note and further wording would be redundant.
